newsitem.title: UK: Amoco says North Sea Halley field "economic".
newsitem.headline: Amoco says North Sea Halley field "economic".

text.p: Amoco (U.K.) Exploration Co said on Monday a new appraisal well at its North Sea Halley field has proven additional reserves making the project commercially viable.

Amoco, which has a 25.77 percent stake in the field, said it was reviewing development options with co-venturers Amerada Hess Corp (28.46 percent), Enterprise Oil Plc (25.77 percent) and Mobil Corp (20.00 percent).

Oil was first discovered at Halley -- in block 30/12b some 140 miles southeast of Aberdeen -- 16 years ago when two wells tested hydrocarbons at significant rates but operator Amoco deemed them uneconomical to develop at the time.
"Technical improvements and the presence of infrastructure nearby prompted Amoco and its co-venturers to reconsider Halley," the company said in a statement.
The latest appraisal well, drilled in 273 feet of water by the Sedco 707 drilling rig, tested hydrocarbons in two zones of the upper Jurassic formation.
The lower zone produced 4,700 barrels per day (bpd) on a 32/64 inch choke, while the upper zone yielded 4,530 bpd.

Industry analysts Wood Mackenzie estimated the field could have reserves of 10 million barrels of oil, adding that it was most likely to be developed via subsea tie-back to the nearby Shell-operated Fulmar field.
